beats.script_body: Journalist Frederick Law Olmsted and architect Calvert Vaux designed the country's first landscaped park here in 1858 to meet a need for urban greenery. As ordinary New Yorkers searched for respite from the nineteenth-century city, members of high society pressed for a dedicated public space in which to socialize, and where the lower classes would benefit from fresh air. After a lengthy debate, an area of Manhattan unsuitable for commercial buildings was chosen as the site. Twenty thousand workers spent twenty years turning swamps into lakes, redesigning the rocky landscape, planting more than 270,000 trees and shrubs, and transforming the whole area into an idyllic pastoral oasis.

beats.source_passage: Journalist Frederick Law Olmsted and architect Calvert Vaux designed the country's first landscaped park in 1858 to meet a need for urban greenery. In the 19th century, as ordinary New Yorkers searched for respite from the city, members of high society began pressing for a dedicated public space in which to socialize, and where the lower classes would benefit from fresh air. After a lengthy debate, an area of Manhattan unsuitable for commercial buildings was chosen as the site of the new park. Twenty thousand workers spent 20 years turning swamps into lakes, redesigning the rocky landscape, planting more than 270,000 trees and shrubs, and transforming the whole area into an idyllic pastoral oasis.

beats.script_body: Central Park stretches south to north from 59th Street to 110th Street, and across from Fifth Avenue to Central Park West. Seen from above, the park's 843 acres form a vast green rectangle — a stark contrast to the density of the skyscrapers that surround it. Inside, you can swim, ice skate, go boating, cycle, walk, or just enjoy the many gardens.

beats.script_body: More than 150 species from around the world live in the Central Park Zoo, including red pandas, grizzly bears, and rare snow leopards. The modern five-acre facility was first established as a makeshift menagerie in 1860, expanded in the 1930s, and refurbished in 1984. Among its highlights are the octagonal sea lion pool in the central courtyard, where daily feedings take place, and the Tisch Children's Zoo, which opened in 1997, where kids get the chance to pet and feed goats, alpacas, Vietnamese pot-bellied pigs, and more.

beats.script_body: The Mall is a long, tree-lined pedestrian walkway where New Yorkers once came to stroll in their Sunday best, and it remains a great place for people-watching. It is flanked by benches and rows of giant American elms forming a leafy canopy that entices photographers to attempt the perfect Central Park shot. The Mall's majestic trees form one of the largest remaining collections of American elms in the country — the rest of the population having been largely wiped out by Dutch elm disease.

It is flanked by benches and rows of giant American elms forming a leafy canopy, enticing many photographers into trying to capture the perfect Central Park shot. Not only visually stunning, the Mall's majestic trees also form one of the largest remaining collections of American elms in the country; the rest of the population has been tlearly wiped out by Dutch elm disease.

beats.script_body: The lake's eastern tip is graced by the elegant Loeb Boathouse, a large, copper-roofed redbrick building that opened in 1954, replacing a Victorian boathouse designed in 1874 by Calvert Vaux. From here you can rent bicycles to tour the park, and rowboats and Venetian gondolas — complete with singing gondoliers — to glide across the eighteen-acre lake, under the gaze of diners on the deck of the Boathouse Restaurant.

beats.script_body: The memorial to musician and songwriter John Lennon is a 2.5-acre, tear-shaped garden across the street from the Dakota building, where Lennon and his wife, Yoko Ono, lived at the time of his murder in 1980. The couple often visited this peaceful stretch of the park, which today draws thousands of fans on the anniversaries of Lennon's birth, October 9, and death, December 8 — many staying late into the night singing his favorite songs. A black-and-white mosaic on the ground bearing the word 'Imagine' marks the heart of the memorial, and a nearby bronze plaque lists the 121 countries that donated trees, plants, and stones to endorse the site as a garden of peace.

beats.script_body: Standing at the highest point in the park, Belvedere Castle offers panoramic views of both greenery and cityscape from its granite towers. When it was built in 1869, it was intended as a whimsical lookout. The National Weather Service has been taking the city's temperature from here every day since 1919. The castle also draws nature enthusiasts: visitors can borrow a free Discovery Kit backpack — containing binoculars, a guidebook, a map, and sketching materials — or join events such as the 'On A Wing' series, which explores the park's many winged creatures.

beats.script_body: Literature lovers should not miss the Shakespeare Garden, a quiet, four-acre spread that abounds with many of the plants mentioned in Shakespeare's poems and plays, including the distinctly Elizabethan-sounding flax and cowslip, primrose, wormwood, quince, and lark's heel. Beautifully landscaped and secluded, it has a twisting, ascending path dotted with rustic wooden benches and bronze plaques inscribed with quotations from the Bard. The garden is especially spectacular in spring, when crocuses, hyacinths, and roses bloom.

Beautifully landscaped and secluded, with a twisting, ascending path dotted with rustic wooden benches and bronze plaques inscribed with quotations from the Bard, the garden is a hidden gem. The garden is especially spectacular in spring, when crocuses, hyacinths, and roses are in bloom.

beats.script_body: This six-acre garden is a popular spot for weddings, thanks to its fairy-tale-like setting, and is composed of three distinct sections: Italian, French, and English. The central, Italian-style garden is a large lawn bordered by two pink-and-white crabapple allées. The French-inspired garden bursts with color when tulips bloom in spring and when chrysanthemums put on their annual show in fall. Circular pathways meander around the English-style garden, where magnolias and Japanese lilac trees perfume the air in spring and summer.

beats.script_body: New York's towering buildings and colorful characters have inspired filmmakers since the 1890s, and more than 200 films feature scenes set in Central Park alone — from the sinister assault on Dustin Hoffman and his girlfriend in 'Marathon Man' to the task-force penguins digging a tunnel to escape the Central Park Zoo in 'Madagascar.' New York was first captured on the silver screen in William Heise's 1896 motion picture 'Herald Square,' but many early Manhattan-set movies were actually shot on California sets — a habit that changed with the 1960s 'New Hollywood' era, when Martin Scorsese, Francis Ford Coppola, and Woody Allen found success with stories shot in the city itself.

beats.source_passage: More than 200 films feature scenes that have been set in Central Park alone, from the sinister assault on Dustin Hoffman and his girlfriend in Marathon Man to the task-force-type penguins digging a tunnel to escape from the Central Park Zoo in Madagascar. Although New York was first captured on the silver screen in William Heise's motion picture Herald Square (1896), many subsequent movies set in Manhattan were shot on California sets— such as Alfred Hitchcock's Rear Window in 1954. This changed with the 1960s "New Hollywood" film era, when filmmakers such as Martin Scorsese, Francis Ford Coppola, and Woody Allen created commercial and critical success with stories revolving around, and shot in, New York.

beats.script_body: New York City opened the country's first bike path in 1894 and now has more than 250 miles of cycling paths, many of them in Central Park. The Manhattan Waterfront Greenway, which circumnavigates the island, is a 32-mile traffic-free path for runners and cyclists; to reach it from Central Park, you ride west directly to the Hudson River.

beats.script_body: Central Park has lanes dedicated to running as well as biking. Every lamp post on the Central Park Loop — the six-mile interior road that encircles the park — is marked with a street number and a 'W' for west or 'E' for east, so you cannot easily get lost. It is considered polite to run counterclockwise around the park's lake.

beats.script_body: Central Park's Lasker Pool, in the northeast corner at 106th Street, is a free outdoor public pool that lets swimmers enjoy views of Manhattan's skyscrapers. To avoid the crowds of splashing children, swimmers can aim for the weekday lap swim, held Monday through Friday in the early morning and evening.
